items.headline: Flood Watch issued November 19 at 2:51AM EST until November 19 at 7:00PM EST by NWS Miami FL
items.description:
Bands of scattered showers and storms, on the north side of
developing low pressure, are expected to move inland across south
Florida today. The highest probability of being impacted by heavy
rain will be across Broward and Palm Beach counties today.

* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...The metros of Miami-Dade and especially Broward and Palm
Beach counties.

* WHEN...Through this evening.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Flooding may occur in poor drainage and urban areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Widespread 3 to 5 inches of rain have fallen across the east
coast of South Florida over the past several days, with pockets
of 8 to 15 inches. Areas having received these higher end amounts
are most susceptible to today's forecast rain amounts. Common
rainfall amounts in locations impacted by showers will be 1 to 2
inches, with the isolated high end amounts closer to 3 to 5
inches.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
items.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be prepared to take action
should Flash Flood Warnings be issued.

items.headline: Rip Current Statement issued November 19 at 2:35AM EST until November 20 at 7:00PM EST by NWS Miami FL
items.description:
* WHAT...Dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...Coastal Miami Dade County.

* WHEN...Through Friday evening.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water.
items.instruction:
Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

items.headline: Small Craft Advisory issued November 19 at 2:35AM EST until November 20 at 1:00PM EST by NWS Miami FL
items.description:
* WHAT...East winds around 25 kts with gusts around 30 kts and
seas 6 to 9 ft.

* WHERE...Coastal waters from Jupiter Inlet to Deerfield Beach
FL out 20 NM, Coastal waters from Deerfield Beach to Ocean
Reef FL out 20 NM, Waters from Jupiter Inlet to Deerfield
Beach FL from 20 to 60 NM and Waters from Deerfield Beach to
Ocean Reef FL from 20 to 60 NM excluding the territorial
waters of Bahamas.

* WHEN...Until 1 PM EST Friday.

* IMPACTS...Conditions will be hazardous to small craft.
items.instruction:
Inexperienced mariners, especially those operating smaller
vessels, should avoid navigating in hazardous conditions.
